reviewMethod: Codex drafting followed by a separate agent editorial review against complete archived source; not independent legal review.

headings.title: Conduct authorized by law or court decree
headings.reviewNote: Retains limits from other law and chapter provisions; covers each of the five listed sources of authority.

headings.title: Reasonable reliance on court or public-servant authority
headings.reviewNote: Distinguishes reasonable belief despite jurisdictional defects or exceeded authority from knowing unlawful conduct.

headings.title: Defendant’s burden to raise justification
headings.reviewNote: Describes injecting the issue, not an ultimate burden of proof.

entries.reviewSummary: Separate Codex editorial pass against the full archived version and notes: Public-duty statutory and court authority, reasonable-reliance exceptions, and issue-injection burden distinguished. This is not independent legal review.

headings.title: Emergency necessity and excluded offenses
headings.reviewNote: Includes imminent injury, absence of actor fault and balancing; class A felonies and murder excluded. No claim that any emergency excuses conduct.

headings.title: Limits on necessity arguments and the court’s ruling
headings.reviewNote: Covers both excluded moral objections to the statute and legal ruling on claimed facts if established.

headings.title: Justification as an affirmative defense
headings.reviewNote: Uses source terminology without inventing the evidentiary standard.

entries.reviewSummary: Separate Codex editorial pass against the full archived version and notes: Emergency necessity excludes class A felonies and murder; judicial gatekeeping and affirmative-defense designation retained. This is not independent legal review.

headings.title: Defensive physical force and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Includes reasonable belief, third-person defense, aggressor exceptions, protected-person limitation and forcible-felony restriction.

headings.title: Conditions for using deadly defensive force
headings.reviewNote: Retains the three alternative conditions and subsection1 context; not an unconditional permission to use force against trespass.

headings.title: Locations where retreat is not required
headings.reviewNote: Covers dwelling, residence, vehicle, owned or leased property and other places the person has the right to be.

headings.title: Protective restraint and ending it
headings.reviewNote: Includes reasonable measures to end restraint as soon as reasonable.

headings.title: Raising justification and the state’s proof burden
headings.reviewNote: Distinguishes defendant issue-injection from the specified state burden when subdivision2 of subsection2 is asserted; does not extend that text to every case.

entries.reviewSummary: Separate Codex editorial pass against the full archived version and notes: Initial-aggressor exceptions, deadly-force conditions, no-retreat locations, restraint, and conditional state proof burden read with veto-override effective-date note. This is not independent legal review.

headings.title: Battered spouse syndrome evidence in defense claims
headings.reviewNote: Names the evidence and defense issue without limiting it to married defendants; read marital-status and self-defense annotations.

headings.title: Advance notice and examination procedures
headings.reviewNote: Includes notice, state motion, qualified examiners, consent to appointment, examination conditions and potential witness interviews.

headings.title: Limits on using examination statements and information
headings.reviewNote: Restriction concerns whether the accused committed the charged act, including later state or federal proceedings; not a blanket statement about all uses.

entries.reviewSummary: Separate Codex editorial pass against the full archived version and notes: Evidence topic is not restricted to married defendants; Williams and Anderson annotations read alongside advance notice, examination, and statement-use restrictions. This is not independent legal review.

headings.title: Physical force to prevent property offenses
headings.reviewNote: Covers stealing, property damage and tampering under reasonable-belief limits; deadly force addressed separately.

headings.title: Deadly force requires other statutory authorization
headings.reviewNote: Makes the cross-reference condition clear without implying protection of property alone authorizes deadly force.

headings.title: Protective restraint and ending it
headings.reviewNote: Requires reasonable measures to terminate restraint when reasonable.

headings.title: Nuclear security guards: force and threats of force
headings.reviewNote: Read all enumerated crimes, deadly versus nondeadly levels, threat authorization and plant-location limits; no inference from crime names alone.

headings.title: Civil liability protection for permitted guard conduct
headings.reviewNote: Includes guard, employer and plant owner, limited to conduct permitted by this section.

headings.title: Defendant’s burden to raise justification
headings.reviewNote: Describes issue-injection, not proof of the entire defense.

entries.reviewSummary: Separate Codex editorial pass against the full archived version and notes: Property offenses and deadly-force cross-reference read separately from nuclear security guards distinct force/threat levels, civil protection, and issue-injection burden. This is not independent legal review.

headings.title: Arrest and escape prevention: force and retreat
headings.reviewNote: Covers resistance, no duty to desist or retreat, and immediately necessary physical force subject to later subsections.

headings.title: Lawful arrest and objectively reasonable force
headings.reviewNote: Retains reasonably believed lawful arrest alternative and totality-of-circumstances standard without regard to motive.

headings.title: Conditions for officers’ use of deadly force
headings.reviewNote: Read both other-chapter authorization and immediately necessary arrest/escape prong with three specified circumstances.

headings.title: Defendant’s burden to raise justification
headings.reviewNote: Preserves injecting-the-issue meaning.

entries.reviewSummary: Separate Codex editorial pass against the full archived version and notes: Lawful-arrest alternative of reasonable belief and objective reasonableness checked; deadly force remains conditional and defendant burden is to raise the issue. This is not independent legal review.

headings.title: Physical force when assisting an officer
headings.reviewNote: Includes reasonable belief about officer status and directions; excludes known or believed unauthorized arrest and remains subject to deadly-force limits.

headings.title: Independent arrests by private persons
headings.reviewNote: Avoids own arrest being read as the private person being arrested; source still requires actual offense and reasonable belief.

headings.title: Conditions for private persons’ use of deadly force
headings.reviewNote: Includes other statutory authority, officer direction with reasonable belief, and specified offenses or escape in the actor’s presence.

headings.title: Defendant’s burden to raise justification
headings.reviewNote: Does not recast issue-injection as proof of the defense.

entries.reviewSummary: Separate Codex editorial pass against the full archived version and notes: Private independent arrest title clarified to avoid implying the actor is being arrested; actual commission plus reasonable belief distinguished from officer-directed assistance and deadly-force alternatives. This is not independent legal review.

headings.title: Physical force to prevent escape from confinement or transit
headings.reviewNote: Limited to guards or other law enforcement officers with reasonable belief of immediate necessity.

headings.title: Conditions for deadly force to prevent escape
headings.reviewNote: Includes other chapter authorization or substantial risk of danger to life or serious injury; not any escape.

headings.title: Defendant’s burden to raise justification
headings.reviewNote: Preserves the burden of injecting the issue.

entries.reviewSummary: Separate Codex editorial pass against the full archived version and notes: Confinement and transit, reasonable-belief requirement for deadly force, and issue-injection burden checked. This is not independent legal review.

headings.title: Care and discipline: conditions and limits on force
headings.reviewNote: Covers entrusted care, welfare or special-purpose discipline and prohibited harm risks; not blanket parental permission.

headings.title: Correctional order and discipline: force authorized by law
headings.reviewNote: The provision references authority elsewhere; does not independently grant unlimited force.

headings.title: Passenger transport: force to prevent interference or maintain order
headings.reviewNote: Includes operator or order-maintenance responsibility and narrower deadly-force condition.

headings.title: Medical treatment: force, consent, and emergencies
headings.reviewNote: Covers medically acceptable treatment, reasonable health purpose, legally competent consent and emergency conditions.

headings.title: Force to prevent suicide or serious self-injury
headings.reviewNote: Names the topic neutrally while retaining reasonable belief and necessity requirements in body.

headings.title: Defendant’s burden to raise justification
headings.reviewNote: Names issue-injection without implying proof of each condition.

entries.reviewSummary: Separate Codex editorial pass against the full archived version and notes: Care, corrections, transport, treatment consent/emergency, and self-injury prevention reviewed separately; limits on force not generalized away. This is not independent legal review.

headings.title: Accidental conduct as an excuse under chapter 565
headings.reviewNote: Includes lawful act and means, absence of knowing injury or attempt, and absence of criminal negligence; not all accidents.

headings.title: Defendant’s burden to raise the accident excuse
headings.reviewNote: Distinguishes excuse from justification and avoids inventing proof burdens.

entries.reviewSummary: Separate Codex editorial pass against the full archived version and notes: Excuse confined to chapter 565, lawful accident and absence of criminal negligence checked; burden remains raising the issue. This is not independent legal review.

headings.title: Qualifying use of force as an absolute defense
headings.reviewNote: Limited to force described in the six referenced sections; does not say all force defeats liability.

headings.title: Civil defense expenses after an absolute-defense finding
headings.reviewNote: Includes attorney fees, costs and reasonable expenses, conditional on court finding in a civil action.

entries.reviewSummary: Separate Codex editorial pass against the full archived version and notes: Absolute defense tied to listed force provisions; civil expense award requires court finding of that defense. This is not independent legal review.
